CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction evaluation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 30-year-old female presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. She reports considering this procedure for approximately 6 to 7 years. Patient reports chronic back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain that have been present since high school. She has been attending chiropractic care for several years with minimal relief. She notes bra strap indentations on her shoulders. Patient occasionally experiences numbness or tingling in her hands. Her breasts are constantly sweaty; she denies rashes underneath her breasts. Activities are limited due to breast size; she must hold her breasts when working out, jumping, or running, which causes pain. Current bra size is G cup; typically wears a 34E sports bra for comfort. Patient would ideally like to be a B cup. She has not pursued physical therapy for back pain. She has not had any mammograms. Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40, and patient has been recommended to start mammograms at age 30. Patient denies interest in breastfeeding but states she may plan to have children in the future. Reports losing approximately 10 pounds over the past few months with a goal to lose approximately 20 more pounds. Denies nipple pain or discharge. Ready to proceed with surgery once new insurance plan is activated, expected in July.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive: Back pain, neck and upper back pain, bra strap indentations on shoulders, occasional numbness or tingling in hands, activity limitations due to breast size. Negative: Rashes underneath breasts, nipple pain, discharge. Notes: Breasts are constantly sweaty. Patient reports overall good health.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
History of migraines.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. Patient advised to begin mammograms at age 30.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Drinks wine occasionally. Denies tobacco and illicit drug use. Currently studying psychology. Works at a desk job.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Bilateral breasts are asymmetrical with severe ptosis bilaterally. One breast is slightly lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable. Measurements obtained. Current breast size approximately G cup.

RESULTS
Body surface area (BSA): 2.65. Schnur scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams. Based on measurements, bilateral reduction mammoplasty appears attainable. Potential for nipple graft given breast size.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
30-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for bilateral breast reduction consultation. Patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Plan includes obtaining photographs today. Once new insurance plan becomes active (expected July), office will submit documentation and photographs to insurance company for approval of medical necessity. Upon insurance approval, office will coordinate surgery date with patient and schedule pre-operative appointment for final review of instructions. Surgical plan: Bilateral reduction mammoplasty using anchor pattern incision extending around nipple downward and underneath. Removal of excess fat and breast tissue with nipple elevation. Target post-operative breast size: small C cup. Estimated operative time: 3 hours. Post-operative plan includes bilateral drain placement (to be removed in clinic after approximately 1 week) and overnight hospital stay. Clear plastic tape to be applied over incisions. Post-operative activity restrictions for approximately 6 weeks including no heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks. Patient counseled on potential complications: approximately 30% risk of inability to breastfeed post-operatively due to removal of glandular tissue, possible alteration or loss of nipple sensation (though generally uncommon unless massive reduction), normal post-operative bruising, scars initially red maturing over approximately 1 year, and breasts may change over time with weight fluctuations and pregnancy. Patient counseled that procedure is a commitment with activity restrictions and encouraged to schedule when she feels ready.
